The last eruption of this caldera was in 762 A.D.

There are two faults that have ruptured in the caldera in the past 76 million years.
The team of scientists say they have found evidence that one of these faults has moved in the past few years.
The other fault hasn’t moved in 10 million years.

The study was published today in Nature Biotechnology and is being presented at the American Society for Gene and Cell Therapy’s 15th Annual Meeting in Washington D.C. It’s not the first time that scientists have tried to manipulate bacteria to treat cancer: but it does take some interesting new directions.
The team took a group of patients who had been treated unsuccessfully for aggressive brain cancer, and gave them intracranially-delivered probiotic bacteria called Lactobacillus rhamnosus: to boost their immune system.
The probiotics were genetically modified so that they would produce an immune-stimulating protein known as granulocyte macrophage colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF). GM-CSF is normally produced by immune cells when they detect foreign invaders like bacteria or viruses.

News of the surgeons’ reprimand, revealed by the Sacramento Bee newspaper, has alarmed bioethicists. “There are a lot of red flags,” says Jonathan Kimmelman of McGill University in Montreal, Canada, who studies the ethics of clinical research.
The case raises tough questions about the standards of evidence that should be met before experimental therapies are tested in people – even those with just weeks to live who may feel that they have nothing to lose.
It also reveals a clash of cultures between surgeons, who are free to try experimental procedures with little regulation, and medical researchers who typically have to present reams of evidence from animal studies before winning approval to test new drugs or biological therapies on human volunteers.

The theme for this year’s observance is “Promoting universal design for accessibility.” Universal design means that products or services are accessible to everyone, regardless of ability or other characteristics.
Universal design is often confused with accessible design, but there are some key differences between these two terms. Accessible design is created to meet specific needs of people who have certain limitations or abilities. For example, an accessible design might be a ramp for people in wheelchairs or braille signage for blind people.
On the other hand, universal design is created for everyone to use comfortably and effectively, without any special adaptations or accommodations. It’s about designing products or services that can be enjoyed equally by all people.
Universal design can be found in everything from homes to workplaces to city streets. Here are a few examples:
• Door handles that are easy to open for people of all ages and abilities
• Kitchens that have plenty of counter space

The best way to assess an investment is to look at the underlying business itself rather than at the investment form.
The key question to ask is:
- Is this business worth investing in?
- And will it generate sufficient returns for me to make my investment worthwhile?
To do this you need to know three things:
- The business model – i.e. how does the business make money?
- The business strategy – i.e what are the plans to make it more profitable?
- The management team – i.e who runs it?
It is also important to be aware that no one investment is safe.
All investment involves some level of risk.
For example, a large multinational business is not immune to the volatility of markets or changes in economic conditions.
A small business has fewer resources to absorb these shocks.
There is no guarantee that an investment will go up in value.

It was first introduced in August last year to support companies that have faced challenges due to the pandemic.
The CIP is being extended to all SMEs that are still affected by the pandemic or have not recovered from it as of today.
The CPM will be available to eligible SMEs from Jan 1 to Sept 30 next year.
The Corporate Income Tax (CIT) rebate will also be extended to eligible SME clients who have been hit hard by the pandemic.
Eligible SMEs can apply for a maximum of 50 per cent of their net taxable profit as a CIT rebate.

Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat, in his Budget statement in Parliament on Monday (Feb 19), also unveiled S$600 million worth of new initiatives, alongside an expansion in the National Robotics Programme (NRP), aimed at harnessing the country’s national research capabilities.
There will be more support for firms to innovate across the entire value chain, according to Mr Heng.
First, to help businesses buy and use new solutions, existing grants supporting the adoption of pre-scoped, off-the shelf technologies will be streamlined into a single Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG).
The PSG will provide funding support of up to 70 per cent of qualifying costs. Businesses can apply for the new grant through the Business Grants Portal (BGP), which will provide a list of supportable equipment and technology solutions relevant for their sectors, from April this year.
